title: Uto-Aztecan Language Family | Language and Linguistics | Research Starters | EBSCO Research
text: There are eight branches: Numic, which includes Northern Paiute, Mono, Monoachi, Koso, Shoshone, Comanche, Ute, Kawaiisu, Southern Paiute, and Chemehuevi; Tubatulabal; Takic, which includes Gabrielino (extinct), Fernandeño, Kitanemuk (extinct), Serrano, Luiseño, Cahuilla, and Cupeño; Hopi; Pimic, which includes Pima, Pima Bajo, Tepecano (extinct), Northern Tepehuan, and Southern Tepehuan; Taracahitic, which includes Tubar (extinct), Tarahumara, Guarijío, Yaqui, Opata, and Cahita; Corachol, which includes Cora and Huichol; and Aztecan, which includes Pochutla (extinct), Pipil, and classical and modern Nahuatl.
